questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to find a University that was English speaking and with good academic opportunities. Furthermore I wanted to find a destination, where there was a big city with lots of university life, but also close to nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright, however I often found the information at the University of Edinburgh quite confusing. Their way of doing things was often quite bureaucratic and old fashioned, and I spent a lot of time both going to and from the University trying to make sure I was doing everything that needed to be done (and doing it correct.)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was quickly put in contact with a student advisor, which was great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If was not easy. I was travelling to Edinburgh with a friend from home, and we found an apartment through "spare room".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it helped us that we were were a bit older (we are both 24 years old), and that we knew each other. I know for a fact that our landlord took this into consideration. It was however not a fun process, as we had to see the apartment over facetime, and kind of just had to trust both our landlord and the whole process. The apartment was big and overall pretty good, and I think we were very lucky (especially when talking to other visiting students about their housing.) Housing in Edinburgh is very expensive, and our apartment was no exception to this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's quite long ago, so I dont remember the specific details. I remember that I was quite puzzled by the fact that I had to fill out information like "religion" and "race". I'm not sure that I think that information such as these is relevant to my registration at the university. Other than that I found it quite easy and alright.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I found help at my home University and the student advisors there.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I was quite succesfull. One of the courses I wanted unfortunately wasn't offered this semester, but otherwise I got the courses I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To find help with the student advisors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found this to be quite mixed. Sometimes the academic level was higher, especially because the we were very few students in the tutorials, so we were expected to discuss the readings and so on every week, and therefore we were also expected to be very prepared. At the same time the level was often similar to my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The tutorial sizes were much much smaller than at UCPH, which was very new to me. I was quite scared of this to start of, since I was expected to discuss reading in English (and in quite an academic way) each week, but I came to enjoy it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Nations and Nationalism, Sociology of Emotions and Mapping Health and Ilness Across Societies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I actually enjoyed all three of my courses, and would particularly recommend both my third year courses (Nations and Nationalism and Sociology of Emotions)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Things that the apartment didn't have. I also spend quite a lot of money going on trips in Scotland, but that was totally worth the costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was cheaper than expected! Overall I found many prices quite similar to DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were alot of societies, however I didn't really participate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on as many trips as possible!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Edinburgh!! Go to the Isle of Skye, go to Cairngorms national park, go hiking around Fort William and Ben Nevis and go to the East coast (we went on a road trip there).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. It helped that Scotland is English speaking. Overall people in Edinburgh and Scotland generally are the loveliest people, and everyone is so sweet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Honestly, I felt very at home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly the Scottish people are!! I also loved the pub culture so much, and in general getting to see Scottish nature and the Highlands was so amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) You are probably going to use more money than you think. At some point during my stay, I just sort of gave up, and enjoyed my time and the trips I went on, instead of thinking too much about expenses. 2) The tutorial sizes at the University of Edinburgh are tiny - so be prepared for that 3) Edinburgh is honestly the best city. It's so walkable and full of students, which is great. Scotland is also so much better than I could have expected. It kept surprising me positively again and again!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just getting to know Edinburgh and Scotland, and getting to know new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge was finding housing, but also getting used to discussing/talking in English (especially in the tutorials)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
